title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Elena Rodriguez
body:
# On-call & Incident Response Playbook

Overview
This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standard incident lifecycle, role definitions, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, on-call rotations, game day guidance, and standard status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, support, and product owners. Follow the procedures below for any outage or degradation impacting latency, throughput, data integrity, or customer-facing errors.

Quick links
- PagerDuty play: Redwood-Core-SRE
- Status page: https://status.redwood-inference.internal (internal)
- Incident board template: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/incident-board-template

Severity definitions and SLO impact
1) Sev 1 (SEV-1) — system down or critical customer impact
   - Symptom: API returns 5xx for large fraction of requests, major data loss, or critical dependency failure.
   - Target response: acknowledge within 5 mins, page primary on-call, target mitigation ETA < 60 mins.
   - Typical SLO impact: significant, immediate notification to leadership.
2) Sev 2 (SEV-2) — major degradation
   - Symptom: high latency for primary endpoints, partial region outage, or large-scale feature regressions.
   - Target response: acknowledge within 15 mins, mitigation ETA 1-4 hours.
3) Sev 3 (SEV-3) — minor user impact or single-customer issue
   - Symptom: a single customer affected, intermittent errors, or non-critical performance regressions.
   - Target response: acknowledge within 4 hours, remediation during regular business hours.
4) Sev 4 (SEV-4) — informational / maintenance
   - Symptom: planned maintenance, low-impact warnings.

Incident lifecycle (high level)
1) Detection & Triage
   - Alerts source: Prometheus, OpenTelemetry traces, customer reports via support, synthetic checks, or automated canaries.
   - On alert, the on-call engineer must:
     1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty within SLAs.
     2. Create an incident in the incident board and assign severity.
     3. Post initial note in the incident channel (#incident-<id>) with summary, impact, and first actions.

2) Containment & Mitigation
   - Follow the relevant service runbook (see Runbooks section).
   - If root cause unknown within first 30 minutes and service is SEV-1/SEV-2, escalate to SRE lead and product owner.
   - Apply temporary mitigations (traffic reroutes, feature flags, rollbacks) before permanent fixes.

3) Communication
   - Internal: update incident channel every 30 minutes for SEV-1, every 60 minutes for SEV-2 until mitigated.
   - External: update status page and customer-facing template (see templates) within 60 minutes for SEV-1 or when customer impact is confirmed.

4) Recovery & Verification
   - Confirm metrics and synthetic checks return to baseline for at least two consecutive evaluation windows (minimum 10 minutes).
   - Validate customer requests and spot-check errors.

5) Post-incident
   - Transition to postmortem within 48 hours.
   - Assign remediation owners, set deadlines, and track in the reliability board.

Roles and responsibilities
- Primary on-call (Engineering on-call): first responder, run runbooks, drive containment.
- Secondary on-call: backup for escalations and timezone coverage.
- SRE Lead / Incident Commander (IC): takes command for SEV-1 incidents, interfaces with leadership.
- Product Owner (PO): clarifies customer impact and business/prioritization decisions.
- Customer Success: owns external notifications for named customers and coordinates follow-ups.
- Communications lead: drafts public-facing status updates for major incidents.

On-call rotations and expectations
- Rotation length: 1 week for Engineering on-call.
- Handoff: 30-minute overlap between shifts with a short handoff doc posted to #oncall-handoffs.
- Time off & coverage: swap requests must be recorded in the on-call schedule; if no swap, follow escalation to secondary on-call.
- Pager responsibilities: acknowledge immediately and act within the severity-specific time windows.
- Burnout policies: no more than 4 consecutive on-call rotations without a recovery week; managers must approve exceptions.

Runbooks (how to use)
- Every production service has a runbook entry under /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/{service-name}. A runbook must include: owner, key metrics, runbook steps, rollback steps, common causes, and post-incident checklists.
- If a runbook is missing, create a minimal stub immediately and mark as required work.

Generic service runbook template (copyable)
- Service: <service-name>
- Owner: <team / on-call alias>
- Key metrics to watch: 5xx rate, p95 latency, request rate, error traces count
- Common alerts: 5xx > 1% sustained (5m), p95 latency > 500ms (5m), queue backlog > 1000
- First response steps:
  1. Confirm the alert: check Grafana dashboard and logs.
  2. Identify scope: single region, multiple regions, single customer.
  3. If configuration or dependency change suspected, check recent deploys (CI/CD) and infra changes.
  4. Apply mitigations: scale up, roll back to previous stable revision, disable feature flag, re-route traffic.
- Rollback steps: CLI example:
  - kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> -n production --to-revision=<rev>
  - Or run: infractl deploy --service <service> --revision <previous>
- Post-incident verification: run synthetic tests and customer smoke tests.

Pager thresholds (recommended)
| Alert | Threshold | Initial severity |
|----|----:|----:|
| API 5xx rate | > 1% sustained over 5m | SEV-2 |
| API 5xx rate | > 5% sustained over 5m | SEV-1 |
| p95 latency (public) | > 500ms over 5m | SEV-2 |
| p95 latency (public) | > 1s over 5m | SEV-1 |
| Cache miss rate | > 20% sustained | SEV-3 |
| Dependency (DB) errors | any increase > 2x baseline | SEV-2 |

Escalation paths
1) Primary on-call -> Secondary on-call (after 15-30 minutes unresolved for SEV-2, immediate for SEV-1).
2) Secondary -> SRE Lead / IC -> VP Engineering if not contained in 60-90 minutes for SEV-1.
3) Product Owner and Customer Success loop in at time of customer impact confirmation.

Incident channel template (first message)
- Title: [INC-<id>] <short description> | <SEV-#>
- Summary: <one-sentence summary>
- Impact: <who/what is affected>
- Start time: <UTC timestamp>
- Actions taken: <bullet list>
- Next steps: <bullet list>
- Owner: <primary-oncall>@redwood

Status page and customer comms templates
- Status page update cadence: initial within 60 minutes for SEV-1, then every 60 minutes until mitigation; for SEV-2 initial within 4 hours.

Customer notification template (short initial)
- Subject: Redwood Inference — Service disruption affecting <feature/region>
- Body:
  Hello <Customer Name>,

  We are investigating an issue affecting <short description>. Our engineering team is actively working to identify the cause and mitigate impact. At this time:
  - Affected services: <list>
  - Estimated impact: <e.g. elevated latency, API errors>
  - Next update: within 60 minutes

  We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a detailed update as we learn more.

  — Redwood Inference Operations

Customer notification template (follow-up / resolution)
- Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident resolved (INC-<id>)
- Body:
  Hello <Customer Name>,

  The incident affecting <services> has been resolved as of <time UTC>. Root cause analysis and postmortem will be shared within 48 hours. If you experienced any lasting issues, please reply to this message and we will prioritize follow-up.

  — Redwood Inference Operations

Postmortem template and expectations
- Timeline: The postmortem must be published within 48 hours for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents. SEV-3 can be published within 5 business days.
- Required fields in the postmortem:
  - Title: INC-<id> — short description
  - Severity
  - Summary (one paragraph)
  - Impact (customers, metrics, duration)
  - Timeline of events (timestamped)
  - Root cause
  - Contributing factors
  - Corrective actions and owner + due dates (actionable)
  - Follow-up (longer-term reliability work)
  - Lessons learned and measurement plan

Postmortem checklist
1. Assign a postmortem owner.
2. Collect logs, traces, and deployment history for the timeline.
3. Interview participants and include citations.
4. Derive at least one actionable remediation with owner and deadline.
5. Publish to /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response and notify stakeholders.

Game days and continuous improvement
- Schedule: at least one cross-team game day per quarter.
- Goals: validate runbooks, test failover procedures, exercise on-call handoffs, and measure detection/mitigation time.
- After-action: publish a short AAR (after action report) with measures and follow-ups.

Operational hygiene & automation priorities
- Keep runbooks in source control and link to services.
- Automate common mitigation patterns (auto-rollbacks, circuit-breakers, canary abort policies).
- Ensure synthetic tests and canaries cover critical user journeys.

Appendix: Useful commands and checks
- Check deployment history: infractl deployments --service <service> --last 10
- Force rollback (example): infractl deploy --service <service> --revision <previous> --force
- Restart workers: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<service> -n production
- Tail logs: kubectl logs -f deployment/<service> -n production --since=15m

Ownership and review cadence
- This playbook is maintained by Eng SRE. Review cadence: quarterly or after any SEV-1 incident.
- To propose changes, open a PR against the confluence source and add reviewers: Eng-SRE, Eng-Platform, Customer Success.
